title: The Diwali Spike

fact_notes: Source for every number: docs/pipeline/2026-11-12/02-account-data.md. Meta Ads account-level numbers, pulled read-only on 12 Nov 2026. 55 accounts listed, 43 readable, 18 kept (spend of at least Rs 5,000 in both September and October, and spend above zero on 9-11 Nov).

Enquiry = a messaging conversation started from the ad (Instagram, Facebook or WhatsApp chat), the largest action in September for all 18 accounts. It is not a booking or an order. The film says so on screen twice.

Rs 147 (1-30 Sep), Rs 165 (1-31 Oct), Rs 210 (1-8 Nov, Diwali week; Diwali was 8 Nov 2026), Rs 164 (9-11 Nov): cost per conversation blended across all 18 accounts (total spend divided by total conversations). Lines 2-3 say 'in our accounts'; the screen says '18 accounts, blended'.
15 of 17 (line 7): cost per conversation, October vs September, rose in 15 of the 17 accounts where both months had at least 10 conversations (median +15.8%). The 18th had too few to compare.

About 5 percent less (line 10), October vs September, median across 18 accounts: CPM -4.7%, cost per link click -5.1%. Pooled CPM also fell (Rs 53 to Rs 48). The screen labels it 'Oct vs Sep, median of 18 accounts'.

A smaller share sent a message (line 11): a rate, not a count. A click cost about 5% less while a conversation cost about 12% more, so fewer conversations came per click. The third bar is labelled 'messages per click'; the bars are an illustration and carry no numbers.

Our reading (line 12) is not a measured cause. It fits the published picture: Redseer via Inc42 (23 Oct 2026), about 100 million shoppers on the big online sales, 8-18 Oct. The card says 'not a measured cause'.
Diwali week vs October (line 13): cost per conversation higher in 13 of 17 accounts, median +26.5%.

13 of 16 (line 14): from Diwali week to 9-11 Nov the cost fell in 13 of 16 accounts (median -17.7%). Rs 164 is the blended figure for all 18, so the line says 'Overall'. Three days of data, 11 to 119 conversations per account.
About October's level, still above September (line 15): Rs 164 vs Rs 165 (October) and Rs 147 (September, about 12% lower).

Close (lines 16-17): -5% is the median account's ad price, +12% is the blended cost per conversation (Rs 147 to Rs 165), both September to October. The claim is limited to October: no Diwali-week click cost was measured, and in the three days after Diwali cost per click was 17.5% above October.
Vertical mix of the 18 accounts: 8 clinics, 3 salons, 2 e-commerce, 5 others. No client or account names appear anywhere in the film or in this folder.
The film does not say ad prices rose, that costs are back to normal, or that performance is better than October.
Independent fact and clarity check, 20 Nov 2026: approve with fixes; all eight fixes applied (period and scope on lines 3, 7, 9-10, 14, 15, 16, 17; 'a smaller share'; the opening question).
